ideas.title: Land yacht: the cart sails on the flow around its own sail
ideas.critique: This answers round 1's main risk: the force on the cloth is the pressure of a re-solved immersed flow, so stall, luffing and the slot come out of the solver and are not fitted, and a player trimming a sheet with friends aboard and the camera beside the lifting wheel breaks the fixed-camera, left-alone form. The danger is the two-way cloth-flow coupling in a box that rides with the cart: if it is unstable or too slow to run live it gets frozen into a lookup, and it still skips the electric road, using only the frame and the wheels.

ideas.title: Kite buggy: a kite you fly pulls the cart across the dune
ideas.critique: Flying figure-eights with two hands while the cart lurches is a strong skill loop, and it uses the same solved-pressure cloth as the land yacht. But it is that idea's twin with a harder problem: a WaterLily box that follows a kite looping fast across a large span will be coarse or lag behind, and the lines and the cart add a second coupled system, so the plainest version is a kite pulling on a rope that leaves the generator drum for later.

ideas.title: Heave: the friends' feet move the stuck cart (road step, sharpened)
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is the road's own next step, now with a berm that grows, feet that dig holes and a rigid cart rocking in its rut, so the stop and the timing come from the physics and not a meter, and that is a real gain over round 1's version. It is still the step anyone would predict next, and as a puzzle it may run out once the timing trick is found.

ideas.title: The friends find out what the wind does to them
ideas.critique: Drag from the solved flow around each creature's own mesh, balanced against foot traction, is a new engine ability that later things can use, and leaning into a gale is good animation work. As a game it is mostly something to watch: the shelter idea is thin, the film is very likely another fixed view of a gale on a crest, and the lean will look scripted unless the gait really answers the force.
